To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a 1-week intensive lifestyle intervention can improve glycemic control in patients with T2DM and 2) this intervention may be most beneficial for patients with T2D who have poor glycemic control at baseline and who have a higher BMI.

1) the majority of patients with T2D who are prescribed a GLP-1 RA have not achieved their glycemic targets, 2) patients with T2d who are prescribed a SGLT2 inhibitor are not meeting their glycemic targets and have high rates of discontinuation, and 3) patients who discontinue a GLP-RA or SGLT2i do not return to the medications.

1) the majority of patients with diabetes are not meeting the American Diabetes Association (ADA) guidelines for glycemic control; 2) there are no differences between patients treated with insulin and those treated with noninsulin agents in terms of achieving the ADA guidelines for glycemic targets; and 3) the majority of diabetes patients are not achieving ADA-recommended lipid and blood pressure targets.
